title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: SharePoint list as a knowledge source in Agent Builder
notes: claim 58: severity blocker on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold for two unsupported statements about permission boundaries: Microsoft does not say permissions apply only to files or guarantee that blocking an agent leaves list permissions unchanged. The roadmap facts, list limits, licensing alternatives and blocking paths are supported; the beta API warning and several governance omissions also need small corrections.

claims.claim: Blocking an agent does not change the SharePoint list's own permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent Builder" "block" "permissions" SharePoint list. Read agent-actions and share-manage-agents. The former says blocking doesn't necessarily revoke connected-service permissions; the latter describes unchanged shared-file access, not list permissions after blocking.
claims.fix: Replace 'Existing alternative: blocking does not change the list's own permissions' with 'Agent approval or blocking does not necessarily grant or revoke connected-service permissions or credentials', as stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-actions.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access reaches the agent access control.
claims.quote:
Open the Microsoft 365 admin center in your browser.
Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: User access offers All users, No users, or Specific users or groups.
claims.quote: Choose All users, No users, or Specific users or groups to control who can access and install agents and plugins.

claims.claim: All users is the default User access option.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: User access controls agent and plugin access rather than Agent Builder creation independently.
claims.quote: This setting controls agent and plugin access, not Agent Builder creation independently.

claims.claim: Agents > Settings > Sharing in the Microsoft 365 admin center reaches org-wide Agent Builder sharing settings.
claims.quote: Org-wide sharing: In Agents > Settings > Sharing, control who can share agents built in Agent Builder with the organization.

claims.quote: Org-wide sharing: In Agents > Settings > Sharing, control who can share agents built in Agent Builder with the organization.

claims.claim: Changes to Sharing settings apply only to new sharing actions.
claims.quote: Changes to the sharing setting apply only to new sharing actions.

claims.claim: Existing shared agents stay accessible after a Sharing setting change unless their sharing settings are manually updated.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a new administrator control specific to SharePoint list grounding in Agent Builder.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent Builder SharePoint list knowledge source admin disable setting Microsoft Graph. Read add-knowledge, agent-settings, agent-actions and share-manage-agents. Results show maker selection and general agent/SharePoint controls, not a list-grounding-specific admin switch.

claims.claim: The cited Restricted Content Discovery page does not explicitly settle selection of SharePoint lists in Agent Builder.
claims.quote: Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or Create pages with AI.
claims.fix: Narrow the question to 'Does this restriction also block the list picker in Agent Builder?' and precede it with 'Microsoft's Manage access to agents in SharePoint page says Restricted Content Discovery prevents adding content from the site to any other agents.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint#turn-off-agents-on-sites-with-restricted-content-discovery alongside the existing source; that page does not explicitly name the Agent Builder list picker.

claims.claim: Microsoft's page says existing permissions apply only for files.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent Builder" "list" "permissions" "only"; Agent Builder SharePoint list knowledge permissions item-level list-level permissions. Read add-knowledge and share-manage-agents. Neither says permissions apply only to files or excludes lists from permission enforcement.
claims.fix: Replace the risk rationale with 'Medium. Makers can point an agent at a list's contents. Microsoft's knowledge page explicitly describes existing permissions for SharePoint and OneDrive files but does not separately explain list-level or item-level enforcement, so test before sharing widely.' Keep https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/agent-builder-add-knowledge as the supporting citation.

claims.claim: Other knowledge-source types have their own documented limits.
claims.quote: Agent Builder supports public websites, SharePoint and OneDrive content, Teams chats and meetings, Outlook email, embedded files, and Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors. Limits vary by source type.

claims.claim: The governance checklist names controls that have no corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Confirm whether Restricted SharePoint Search is enabled in the tenant; Confirm which users hold a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence and whether pay-as-you-go billing is enabled; Decide who may share Agent Builder agents; Watch Copilot Credits consumption. The table contains only agent blocking.
claims.fix: The Restricted SharePoint Search, licence/billing, Sharing and consumption-check steps have no table rows. Without adding rows, remove the first, third and consumption-check bullets; replace the licence/billing bullet with 'Tell agent owners that SharePoint knowledge requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence or tenant usage-based billing, as described under Cost and licensing.'
